insight.title: Why Searching for One Thing Makes You Miss Everything Else
insight.subtitle: How a narrow focus makes you ignore obvious opportunities

sections.text: Watch a hawk hunting mice and you'll see it fly right past a larger, slower rabbit. It has developed a "search image"—a mental filter that ignores anything that doesn't fit the immediate target.

Your brain does this too. When you focus intensely on a specific goal, you stop seeing information that doesn't match your expectations. You aren't just ignoring distractions; you are becoming blind to better opportunities.
We do this with problems, searching for one specific fix or a single person’s approval. By locking onto what you think the solution looks like, you accidentally hide every other path to success.
Try this today: When you look for an answer today, ask if you’ve already decided what it looks like.
The most valuable things are often the ones you aren't currently looking for.
